The batch is the five entries of corrections.toml with batch = T-egf-correct-families. All five are adopted: C-28 under DEC-141, DEC-144 and DEC-187; C-31, C-33 and C-49 under DEC-141; C-32 under DEC-141 and DEC-187. I read the anchors with their statements, binders, docstrings and SCOPE blocks in lean-egf/EGF/TorusFamilies.lean, ToriMinimal.lean, SphereFamilies.lean and SphereDense.lean. From UniversalityErgodic.lean I used universality_of_ergodic_family and isKernelErgodic_egfKernel_uniform. None of the four family files has a sorry, and EGF.lean imports all of them. tools/corrections.py check reports 49 entries, all rules hold. I compared each applied text with the register's `corrected`, after whitespace normalization: (a) verbatim: Theorem 3.6 (l.329), C-28's l.836 (l.890), C-28's l.818-820 (l.870), C-32's theorem (l.884) and its added paragraph (l.887); (b) C-49's l.307 (l.333) is verbatim and is followed by the kept Breuillard sentence with C-33's index; (c) C-28's l.293 (l.316) is verbatim for its first sentence, and the rest of the v1 line is kept; (d) Theorem 3.5 (l.312) is verbatim up to 'for the minimal four moves'. entries.notes:
Theorem 3.5 (l.312) against EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic (A, hA, b, herg, F, hrich), hypothesis by hypothesis:
- Moves in Aff(T^d) with linear part in SL_d(Z). The Lean takes IsUnit (A i).det (GL_d(Z)), which is weaker, so Lean >= paper.
- 'The group generated by the (Phi_i) acts ergodically on (T^d, lambda)'. This is herg : IsGroupErgodic volume (torusAffineGroup A b hA). The group is the closure of the moves in Equiv.Perm, and every measurable set a.e.-invariant under all its elements is null or conull. volume on UnitAddTorus (Fin d) is Lebesgue.
- 'Its model realizes the uniform policy alpha^i = 1/p and a set of outflows dense in the non-negative cone of L^2(S, lambda)'. This is hrich : IsRichToroidalModel A b F: the uniform kernel of the moves at the same b, paired with every f of a set D with IsDenseNonnegConeL2 volume D. Finding 6 covers the wording.
- No algebraicity, no inverse-stability, no spectral gap and no named Prop appear in the Lean, and the TeX asks for none.
- 'An affine toroidal family'. The Lean takes F to be any set of generative flows, so affineToroidalFamily A M is an instance.
- 'A universal EGF family'. This is IsUniversalFamilyEps volume F, the epsilon-form of Definition 3.2 (probability distributions with bounded densities).

Each sufficient condition is anchored:
(a) No invariant factor torus with amenable projection. This is the negation of BGConditionII (linearParts (torusAffineGroup A b hA)). It is EGF.universality_tori under the named Prop BekkaGuivarchTheorem5 d, which the TeX cites as 'Theorem 5 of bekka2015spectral' (DEC-187). The group is countable (countable_torusAffineGroup), and the step from the gap to ergodicity is EGF.ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap.
(b) The group contains an affine map whose linear part has no periodic integer vector. This is EGF.universality_tori_of_mem_noPeriodic (B in linearParts of the group; NoPeriodicVector B means A^n k != k for k != 0 and n >= 1). The ergodicity step is EGF.ergodic_torusAffine_of_noPeriodic (any translation) with EGF.isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem.
  The e.g.: T(STS^{-1})^{-1} = TST^{-1}S^{-1} = [[2,1],[1,1]] (EGF.matT_mul_matS_mul_inv; I also checked it by hand). The commutator Phi_T Phi_S Phi_T^{-1} Phi_S^{-1} lies in the group for every choice of the translations (EGF.mem_torusAffineGroup_commutator, EGF.catMat_mem_linearParts), and EGF.noPeriodicVector_catMat holds. The four moves S^{+-1}, T^{+-1} are EGF.minimalMoves = ![matS, matS^-1, matT, matT^-1], and EGF.universality_tori_minimal holds for every b.
(c) On T^1, a translation of infinite order in the group. This is proved by composing declarations, not by a single one (finding 5).

l.316 (v1 l.293):
- 'For d >= 2, if the group generated by the linear parts is the whole SL_d(Z)' is EGF.universality_tori_sl, with hd : 2 <= d. Its hgen puts SL_d(Z) inside the closure of the A_i as units, i.e. 'contains', which is weaker than 'is'. It holds for every b.
- The d = 2 parenthetical is EGF.coe_mem_linearParts_of_mem_closure with EGF.noPeriodicVector_catMat (EGF.universality_tori_two_of_specialLinearGroup).
- 'For d = 1 if one translation part is irrational' is EGF.universality_tori_one with EGF.addOrderOf_coe_eq_zero_of_irrational. In the paper's setting SL_1(Z) = {1}, so every move is a translation and the Lean's hAi : A i = 1 holds.
- The restriction to d >= 2 answers EGF.not_universality_tori_sl_one.
- The kept 'Therefore, in any dimension ... p = 4' is true, because 'well-chosen' covers the translations (answers.l316_any_dimension).

l.870 (v1 l.818-820): not (ii) gives a spectral gap (spectral_gap_tori from the named Prop). The gap gives ergodicity through the invariant mean-zero 1_A - lambda(A), which is the vector EGF.ergodic_of_hasSpectralGap uses. The uniform policy is then ergodic for lambda (EGF.isKernelErgodic_torusUniformKernel_iff), and Theorem B.1 applies (universality_of_ergodic_family, with Theorem 3.5's richness). Inverse-stability is not used (EGF.universality_tori). Its last sentence, 'Our technical condition of Theorem 3.5 is then ...', is finding 7.

l.890 (v1 l.836): EGF.universality_sphere and EGF.isGroupErgodic_sphereRotGroup_of_dense, with 2 <= n and n = d+1.

findings.what:
In the paper's own notation, the newly quoted Theorem B.3 is vacuous.
- l.880 (unchanged) reads: 'a real number x in R is algebraic if ... The set of algebraic real number is denoted Q-bar'. Q-bar's only use in v2 is the new l.884: g_1, ..., g_k in SU(d) intersect Mat_{dxd}(Q-bar).
- A matrix of SU(d) with real entries is orthogonal of determinant 1. So the g_j lie in SO(d), a closed proper subgroup of SU(d) for d >= 2 (diag(i, -i, 1, ...) is not in SO(d)).
- The group they generate is therefore never dense in SU(d), and the theorem's hypotheses can never be met.

Bourgain and Gamburd, and the named Prop EGF.BourgainGamburdTheorem1, take complex algebraic entries (IsAlgebraic Q of the complex entries). Their hypotheses can be met (EGF.bourgainGamburd_hypotheses_witness, su2Witness, whose entries are not real). So the theorem titled 'Theorem 1 of Bourgain & Gamburd (2012)' is not their theorem. That defeats C-32's purpose ('quoted as its authors state it') and DEC-187's faithful named Props, and the contrast with the failing SO(2) analogue at l.887 loses its point.

This is not an overclaim: the vacuous statement is implied by the Lean's. But the batch creates it. v1's reformulation applied Q-bar to matrices of SO(d), which are real, so v1's real definition fitted it. l.828 is outside C-32's printed lines, so the corrector rightly left it alone.

This settles the corrector's open point: major, for this batch's round 2.

findings.what:
Theorem 3.5's last clause says the group 'contains ... on T^1, a translation of infinite order'. EGF.universality_tori_one instead takes a move (A i = 1, addOrderOf (b i 0) = 0).

The element form is proved by composing three declarations of the strict library, not by a single one. Take h in torusAffineGroup A b hA with h = torusAffine 1 c and addOrderOf (c 0) = 0. Then:
1. EGF.ergodic_torusAffine_one_dim_one gives Ergodic (torusAffine 1 c) volume;
2. EGF.isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem gives IsGroupErgodic for the group;
3. EGF.universality_tori_of_ergodic concludes.
EGF.universality_tori_of_mem_translation is the same composition in every dimension, with the Kronecker condition; on T^1, infinite order gives that condition inside ergodic_torusAffine_one_dim_one. Since the clause is a sufficient condition for ergodicity ('this holds when'), steps 1 and 2 suffice. 'A translation of infinite order', as a group element, means c has infinite additive order.

So nothing is missing from what is proved. The gap is in what the register names: neither isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem nor ergodic_torusAffine_one_dim_one is in C-28's anchor.
findings.fix: In the register, add EGF.isGroupErgodic_of_ergodic_mem, EGF.ergodic_torusAffine_one_dim_one and EGF.universality_tori_of_mem_translation to C-28's anchor. findings.what:
C-28's adopted wording is loose on two points. Neither is an overclaim under the natural reading.
(a) 'Its model realizes the uniform policy alpha^i = 1/p and a set of outflows dense in ...'. The Lean (IsRichToroidalModel, IsRichSphericalModel) needs the outflows paired with the uniform policy, as Theorem 3.4 (l.292) and C-31's own text ('together with') say. If 'and' is read as two separate realizations, the TeX hypothesis is weaker than the Lean's.
(b) The translation parts (tori) and the rotations (spheres) are parameters of the family (l.308, l.326). The Lean fixes one b (or one Phi) and asks both the richness and the ergodicity (or density) there. The TeX can be read three ways:
- At every parameter, as TorusFamilies' SCOPE read v1. The hypothesis is then stronger, every member is an EGF in Definition 3.1's sense, and 'universal EGF family' holds.
- With ergodicity at one parameter and richness at another. The statement is then false. Example on T^1: a family with dense outflows at translation 0 and a single flow at translation sqrt 2.
- At the parameter that realizes the uniform policy. That is the Lean's statement, but 'EGF family' then claims nothing about the other members, which need not be EGFs.

findings.what:
Theorems 3.5 and 3.6 now state their assumptions, but the sentences around them still refer to unnamed ones:
- l.316: 'The `technical assumptions' above are in particular satisfied'. It quotes a phrase that no longer appears above.
- l.333: 'The technical assumption is satisfied if the Phi_i are frozen and generate a dense subgroup'. Theorem 3.6's assumption is that density itself.
- l.890: 'With the technical condition ...'.

All of these are C-28's and C-49's adopted wording, and none is an overclaim.

v2 gives no argument for three of the new ergodicity criteria:
- An affine map whose linear part has no periodic integer vector is ergodic. (Fourier: an invariant L^2 function has |f^(A^T k)| = |f^(k)| along an injective orbit, so f^(k) = 0 for k != 0.)
- On T^1, a translation of infinite order is ergodic (Kronecker/Weyl).
- Rotations generating a dense subgroup of SO_{d+1}(R) act ergodically on S^d. (An a.e.-invariant set is invariant under the closure, SO_{d+1}(R), which is transitive for d >= 1.)

The pointers do not lead to an argument either:
- l.333 points to 'Appendix~B.3', where l.890 only restates the conclusion.
- l.887, which is inside B.3, points to 'Appendix~B.3', i.e. to itself.
- Theorem 3.5's clauses (b) and (c) point nowhere.
- l.316's 'Appendix~B.2' finds only the Bekka-Guivarc'h route there.

All three criteria are proved in Lean, so the paper claims nothing beyond the anchors. What is missing is the paper's proof text, and the pointers are this batch's.
